definitions.definition: The set of letters used when writing in a language.
A writing system in which there are letters for the consonant and vowel phonemes. (Contrast e.g. abjad.)

A writing system in which letters represent phonemes. (Contrast e.g. logography, a writing system in which each character represents a word, and syllabary, in which each character represents a syllable.)
(computer science) A typically finite set of distinguishable symbols.
(India, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia) An individual letter of an alphabet; an alphabetic character.

quote.citation: 2002, Eugene E. Dike, African myth of creation in African form of writing, Monsenstein und Vannerdat, →ISBN, page 30:
quote.text: We realize the fact that the alphabet A has been used in many world scripts as a vowel with the others AEIOU.

quote.citation: 2005, Satinder Bal Gupta, Comprehensive Discrete Mathematics & Structures, Laxmi Publications, page 237:
1828, Thomas Babington Macaulay, “The Constitutional History of England: From the Accession of Henry VII, to the Death of George II, by Henry Hallam”, in The Edinburgh Review, volume 18:
quote.text: The very alphabet of our law.

definitions.definition: (Internet slang, politics) An agent of the FBI, the CIA, or another such government agency.
(rare) To designate by the letters of the alphabet; to arrange alphabetically.
